question: In pre-renal AKI, the renal tubular cells are structurally intact and the kidney will rapidly recover once adequate perfusion is restored.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Pre-renal AKI is a haemodynamic, functional disorder — tubular architecture is intact. Restoration of perfusion corrects it promptly. In contrast, intrinsic AKI (e.g., ATN) involves structural tubular injury and slower recovery.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Pre-renal AKI is a functional state — tubular integrity is preserved, and prompt correction of the perfusion deficit (volume resuscitation, treating cardiac failure, stopping nephrotoxins) leads to rapid recovery. This distinguishes it from established intrinsic AKI (ATN) where tubular cells are injured.
